items: Apply for visa and gather required documents (passport, university admission letter, bank statements)
Book accommodation near campus or join student housing Facebook groups
Check vaccination requirements and schedule any needed immunizations
Purchase international health insurance or check coverage through your university
Open an international bank account or arrange forex exchange
Research phone plans and SIM card options in your destination country
Book your flight and arrange airport pickup or transportation
Notify your bank about travel dates to avoid fraud blocks on cards
Get travel insurance that covers luggage, trip cancellation, and emergency evacuation
Submit any final documents to your university (registration, proof of accommodation)
Arrange mail forwarding for your home address if needed
Purchase adapter plugs and voltage converters for your electronics
Confirm flight details and check-in 24 hours before departure
Pack essentials: medications, documents, university IDs, and one set of business clothes
Download offline maps of your university and city on your phone
Take photos of important documents and store copies in cloud storage
Transfer emergency contact information to your phone
Charge all devices and pack chargers and power banks
Register with your embassy or consulate in the country
Complete university registration and collect your student ID
Set up a local phone plan and top-up your prepaid account
Open a local bank account within the first week if you haven't already
Attend student orientation and join clubs or societies
Get familiar with public transportation and buy a student transport card if available

USA.detail: Your university issues the I-20 form confirming your acceptance and financial support.

USA.step: Pay SEVIS fee (Student and Exchange Visitor Program)
USA.detail: Pay the $350 SEVIS fee online and receive the payment receipt (required for visa application).

USA.step: Apply for F-1 visa at US embassy or consulate
USA.when: After SEVIS payment, at least 1 month before travel
USA.detail: Submit DS-160 form, pay visa fee ($185), and schedule an interview at your nearest US embassy.
Bring I-20, SEVIS receipt, passport, bank statements, and university admission letter. Demonstrate ties to your home country.
Your visa will be stamped in your passport. Valid for the duration of status (D/S).

USA.step: Arrival at US port of entry
USA.when: Within the validity period on your I-20
USA.detail: Expect questioning about your field of study, financial support, and return plans. Carry all documents.
Register with your university's international office to confirm your status and receive updates.

UK.step: Receive Confirmation of Acceptance for Studies (CAS)
UK.detail: Your university issues a CAS letter confirming your admission and financial sponsorship.

UK.when: After receiving CAS, at least 3 weeks before travel
UK.detail: Submit your Student visa application (Subclass SK) on the UK Visas and Immigration website.

UK.when: As part of online visa application
UK.detail: Pay approximately GBP 1,035 per year (or GBP 719 for postgraduates) for access to NHS healthcare.
Visit a UK Visas and Immigration service point to provide your biometric information.
You will receive a Biometric Residence Permit (BRP) card in the post or at a collection point.
Enter the UK with your passport and CAS letter. Keep BRP card safe as proof of status.

UK.step: Register with your university and local police (if required)
UK.detail: Some universities and police stations require international student registration for record-keeping.

Canada.step: Receive Letter of Acceptance from your institution
Canada.when: After being accepted to a Canadian school
Canada.detail: Your college or university issues this letter confirming your admission and meets DLI requirements.
Prepare passport, Letter of Acceptance, proof of funds (CAD 20,000-30,000), and medical exam results.

Canada.step: Pass medical exam from approved physician
Canada.detail: Book a medical examination with a panel physician approved by Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canada (IRCC).

Canada.step: Create an online account and apply for study permit
Canada.when: At least 4 months before your start date
Canada.detail: Submit your application through the Government of Canada website with all required documents.

Canada.when: As part of study permit application
Canada.detail: Pay CAD 150 online for study permit processing.
You will receive your study permit approval document or physical permit at the port of entry.

Canada.step: Arrival at Canadian port of entry
Canada.when: On or before your course start date
Canada.detail: Present your passport, study permit approval, and Letter of Acceptance to immigration officials.

Australia.when: After enrollment is finalized at your Australian institution
Australia.detail: Your university issues a CoE certifying your enrolment and confirming your place in a course.
Prepare passport, CoE, proof of financial capacity (AUD 25,000+), and evidence of English proficiency.

Australia.step: Pass health examination and police checks
Australia.detail: Complete medical exams at a panel doctor and obtain police certificates from your home country.
Pay approximately AUD 650 per year for required health insurance during your stay.

Australia.when: At least 3 months before intended arrival
Australia.detail: Use the online portal to lodge your application with all supporting documents.
You will receive an electronic Confirmation of Visa Granted, allowing you to travel to Australia.

Australia.when: On or before your course start date
Australia.detail: Present your visa and CoE at Australian border control. Register with your university within the first week.

Germany.step: Receive admission letter from German university
Germany.when: After being accepted to a German institution
Germany.detail: Your university issues the formal admission letter required for visa application.

Germany.step: Open blocked account or proof of funds
Germany.detail: Deposit approximately EUR 11,208 in a blocked account or show proof of financial support.
Prepare passport, admission letter, proof of funds, health insurance documentation, and language certificate (if required).

Germany.step: Apply for German student visa at embassy or consulate
Germany.when: At least 2-3 months before intended start date
Germany.detail: Submit your application at the German embassy in your home country with all required documents.
Attend an interview to confirm your intentions, financial capacity, and language ability (if applicable).
Your visa will be stamped in your passport, valid for entry into Germany and residence permit processing.

Germany.step: Register with Auslanderbehorde (immigration office) upon arrival
Germany.when: Within 3 months of arriving in Germany
Germany.detail: Complete your residence permit registration at the immigration office in your university city.

cityGuides.intro: London is a vibrant global hub with world-class universities and diverse student communities. The city offers excellent museums, parks, and cultural events, though accommodation and dining can be expensive.
cityGuides.cost: GBP 1,400-1,800 per month (accommodation GBP 700-1,200, food GBP 250-400, transport GBP 150, entertainment GBP 200-300)
cityGuides.transport: Students rely on the London Underground (Tube), buses, and the Oyster Card for affordable weekly travel passes. Many universities offer student railcards for discounts on national trains.
tips: Join your university's student union and attend freshers' events to meet people
Use Tesco and Sainsbury's Nectar cards for grocery discounts
Explore free museums (British Museum, National Gallery, V&A Museum) with your student ID
Buy a 16-25 railcard for 30% off national train fares
Live in areas like Stratford, Southwark, or Clapham for affordability with good transport links
studentAreas: Bloomsbury (near UCL, great for academics and culture)
South Kensington (near Imperial and RCA, expensive but vibrant)
Clapham (trendy, good nightlife, slightly south of central London)

cityGuides.intro: Toronto is Canada's largest city with major universities and a multicultural vibe. It offers excellent job opportunities, diverse neighborhoods, and a strong international student community despite cold winters.
cityGuides.cost: CAD 1,600-2,100 per month (accommodation CAD 900-1,300, food CAD 300-400, transport CAD 150, entertainment CAD 250-400)
cityGuides.transport: The Toronto Transit Commission (TTC) operates subway, streetcars, and buses. Students get discounted Metropass fares (around CAD 56/month) and universities offer additional transit benefits.
tips: Buy a winter coat early—temperatures drop to -10°C in January
Get a PRESTO card for seamless TTC payment across all transit
Explore Kensington Market and St. Lawrence Market for affordable groceries
Join university clubs and attend orientation events to build your social network
Look for student housing in Chinatown, Kensington, or near your campus for best prices
studentAreas: University District (near U of T, walkable and vibrant)

cityGuides.intro: Sydney combines stunning beaches, outdoor culture, and world-class universities. It's an excellent place to study with great weather most of the year, though accommodation and living costs are high.
cityGuides.cost: AUD 2,000-2,600 per month (accommodation AUD 1,200-1,600, food AUD 350-500, transport AUD 180, entertainment AUD 270-400)
cityGuides.transport: Opal Card provides discounted fares on trains, buses, ferries, and light rail. Student cards offer 50% off most journeys, and ferries are an affordable way to travel while enjoying the harbor.
tips: Get an Opal card immediately upon arrival for cheapest public transport
Visit Bondi, Coogee, and Manly beaches on weekends—many are free
Join university clubs and student organizations for social events and networking
Shop at Aldi and Woolworths for budget groceries
Check out free events like Open-air cinema, live music, and food festivals in summer
studentAreas: Newtown (bohemian, affordable, great cafes and nightlife)
Glebe (near University of Sydney, leafy, trendy shops)

cityGuides.intro: Berlin is one of Europe's most affordable capitals for students, with cutting-edge art, music, and tech scenes. It offers excellent value for money and a youthful, international atmosphere perfect for studying abroad.
cityGuides.cost: EUR 850-1,200 per month (accommodation EUR 450-700, food EUR 200-300, transport EUR 30, entertainment EUR 170-200)
cityGuides.transport: BVG operates an efficient subway, tram, and bus network. Student discounts are available, and a monthly pass costs around EUR 30 for Berlin's ABC zones, making it very affordable.
tips: Get a BVG student monthly pass for EUR 30—one of Europe's cheapest transit deals
Eat at student canteens (Mensen) affiliated with your university for cheap, filling meals
Visit free museums on Thursdays after 6 PM and explore Berlin's street art scene
Use Flixbus for affordable travel to other European cities on weekends
Explore vintage shops, flea markets, and beer gardens—Berlin's culture is affordable

cityGuides.intro: New York City offers world-class universities and unmatched career opportunities, but comes with high costs. The diverse neighborhoods and cultural attractions make it exciting despite the expense and fast-paced environment.
cityGuides.cost: USD 2,400-3,200 per month (accommodation USD 1,300-1,800, food USD 400-600, transport USD 133, entertainment USD 300-500)
cityGuides.transport: The MTA operates the subway (the fastest way to get around) and buses. Students get a reduced MetroCard fare (around USD 27/week) making the subway affordable for daily commutes.
tips: Buy a 7-day or 30-day MetroCard to save on subway and bus fares
Use your student ID at restaurants and museums for discounts
Explore affordable neighborhoods like Astoria (Queens), Sunset Park (Brooklyn), and Washington Heights (Manhattan)
Join your university's clubs and student organizations immediately—social life is key
Use Citi Bike for short trips and weekend exploring at just USD 15/month for students
studentAreas: Morningside Heights / Harlem (near Columbia, vibrant culture, affordable)
Astoria, Queens (affordable, diverse, good transport to Manhattan)
Washington Heights (very affordable, residential, good subway access)

cityGuides.intro: Dublin is a vibrant, English-speaking destination with excellent universities and a legendary social scene. It offers a blend of historical charm and modern culture, though prices have risen in recent years.
cityGuides.cost: EUR 1,200-1,700 per month (accommodation EUR 700-1,000, food EUR 250-350, transport EUR 80, entertainment EUR 170-300)
cityGuides.transport: Dublin Bus and Luas (light rail) are the main systems. A student leap card costs around EUR 20-25/week and works on all public transport, including taxis and ferries.
tips: Get a Leap Card (student version) for discounted transport across all modes
Visit Temple Bar (busy and touristy) but explore quieter pubs in other neighborhoods
Shop at Aldi, Lidl, and Dunnes Stores for budget groceries
Explore free attractions like Trinity College campus, St. Stephen's Green park, and the Guinness Storehouse discounts with student ID
Attend university events and pub quizzes—Dublin's social scene revolves around pubs
studentAreas: Ballymun and Drumcondra (affordable, residential, good bus links)
Temple Bar area (vibrant but pricey, full of tourists)
Stoneybatter (trendy, emerging food scene, good pubs)

cityGuides.intro: Repeatedly ranked among the worlds best student cities, Melbourne mixes top universities with great coffee, sport and a huge international community.
cityGuides.transport: Free tram zone in the CBD; get a Myki card for trams, trains and buses.
tips: Apply for student accommodation early — it goes fast near campus.
Your student visa lets you work up to 48 hours per fortnight.
Use the free City Circle tram to get around the centre.
Open a local bank account and get a Myki concession if eligible.

cityGuides.intro: Home to UBC and SFU, Vancouver offers world-class study with mountains and ocean on your doorstep — beautiful, but plan for high housing costs.
cityGuides.transport: SkyTrain, SeaBus and buses with a Compass Card; a U-Pass is included at many universities.
tips: Start your housing search months ahead — Vancouver rent is high.
A study permit usually allows up to 24 hours/week of off-campus work.
Get a U-Pass through your student union for cheap transit.
Layer up and carry a rain jacket — winters are wet, not freezing.

cityGuides.intro: A friendly, affordable UK student city with two big universities, legendary music and football, and one of the largest student populations in Europe.
cityGuides.transport: Buses and the Metrolink tram; get a student travel card for discounts.
tips: Fallowfield is the classic student area — book a house share early.
A Student visa allows up to 20 hours/week of work in term time.
Use a 16–25 Railcard for cheap trips to London and beyond.
Council tax is usually exempt for full-time students.

cityGuides.intro: Munich pairs top tuition-free public universities (TUM, LMU) with high quality of life — safe, green and a gateway to the Alps.
cityGuides.transport: Excellent U-Bahn, S-Bahn, tram and bus network; the Deutschlandticket (€49/month) covers regional transport nationwide.
tips: Public universities charge little or no tuition — budget mainly for rent.
You need a blocked account (Sperrkonto) for your student visa.
Apply for student dorms (Studentenwerk) very early — demand is high.
Register your address (Anmeldung) within two weeks of arriving.
